translations.text: What does it mean when carrot seeds fail to sprout

When carrot seeds sown in soil fail to emerge for an extended period or seedlings gradually or suddenly die back, it is usually a combination of unfavorable environmental conditions in the soil crust that is responsible. Carrots have very small seeds, and shallow planting depth combined with high sensitivity to cold soil, surface drying, and crusting causes germination failure in many gardens
In the source region, carrot seed planting is considered permissible only after soil temperature has reached a minimum of 40 °F; below this threshold, growth does not begin
. Optimal germination temperature is reported between 55 and 65 °F, and within this range, emergence takes approximately 14 to 21 days

When the soil surface seals and hardens after irrigation or rain, carrot seedlings, due to their small size and limited energy, are unable to penetrate the crust. In this case, emergence is restricted and plant structure is damaged
After emergence, soil moisture fluctuations cause root disorders, slow leaf growth, and bitter taste in carrots
. Additionally, alternating wet and dry periods promote carrot root cracking
. For this reason, maintaining uniform surface soil moisture is recommended to ensure carrot plant stand stability
Before planting, measure soil temperature; if it is below 40 °F, wait.
At temperatures of 55 to 65 °F, expect emergence in 14 to 21 days.
Prevent surface crusting; keep the surface soft with gentle irrigation or light sprinkling.
Maintain uniform surface moisture to prevent root disorders and bitter taste.
When temperatures exceed 80 °F, germination decreases and planting should be done with greater caution.

All numerical observations in this article are extracted from one academic source (Utah State University Extension) and their geographic scope is Utah and the semi-arid climate of the United States. Units are reported exactly as °F and days, and no recommendations for conditions in Iran have been derived
Why don't carrot seeds green? An examination of temperature, moisture, and soil crusting
Carrot seeds do not green easily; low soil temperature, surface crusting, and moisture fluctuations are the three main obstacles facing carrot germination and poor stand establishment.
Why do carrot seeds fail to emerge after planting?

In the evidence from the source region, carrot seeds fail to green when soil temperature has not yet reached a minimum of 40 °F; under these conditions, growth has not begun and germination remains halted source.
How long does it take for carrot seed to emerge at suitable temperatures?
At an optimal temperature of 55 to 65 °F, carrot seedling emergence takes 14 to 21 days source.
When do soil moisture fluctuations prove detrimental to carrots?
Soil moisture fluctuations cause root disorders, slow leaf growth, and bitter taste in carrots; additionally, alternating wet and dry periods exacerbate root cracking source.
